shortcut_name: incidence-vector span reduces to Steiner connectivity
evidence: "dp[mask][v] = min cost to connect terminals in mask, ending at node v"; "We want to connect all focal dimensions with minimum cost"
affordance_in_statement: "Each available generator vector is of the form e_u - e_v" and "the linear span W ... contains the required e_i - e_j vectors"; additionally, vectors may involve "non-focal dimensions".
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: selected vectors e_u-e_v span exactly the differences within connected components of the selected graph. Hiding the graph interpretation would only obscure, not remove, the affordance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Models each generator as a weighted graph edge and applies subset dynamic programming for the weighted Steiner tree.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: "dp[mask][v] = min cost to connect terminals in mask, ending at node v"

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the same graph-Steiner formulation with terminal-subset DP and shortest-path relaxation.

common_affordance: The equivalence between choosing vectors e_u-e_v whose span contains all focal differences and choosing a minimum-cost connected subgraph spanning the focal vertices, allowing non-focal Steiner vertices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Restricts the optimization to an MST on focal dimensions and does not correctly allow non-focal vertices to act as shared Steiner points.
Uses shortest-path distances followed by a terminal MST-style construction, which can double-count shared non-focal portions and is not generally equivalent to the Steiner tree optimum.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat both surviving models without changing the mathematical task: the graph-connectivity equivalence is the intrinsic structure of the stated problem. Any successful defeat would require changing the generator vectors or the span requirement, which changes the problem.
